messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:
L1: PPhtBu2 [SMILES CC(C)(C)P(C1=CC=CC=C1)C(C)(C)C]
L2: BrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C1=CC(C(C)C)=C(C(C(C)C)=C1)C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L3: X-Phos [SMILES CC(C1=C(C2=CC=CC=C2P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C(C(C)C)=CC(C(C)C)=C1)C]
L4: GorlosPhos HBF4 [SMILES CC(OC1=C(P(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3)C(OC(C)C)=CC=C1)C]
L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L6: PPhMe2 [SMILES CP(C)C1=CC=CC=C1]
L7: PPh2Me [SMILES CP(C1=CC=CC=C1)C2=CC=CC=C2]
L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]
S4: n-butyl acetate [SMILES CCCCOC(C)=O]

concentration:
C1: 0.057 M
C2: 0.1 M
C3: 0.153 M

temperature:
T1: 90 °C
T2: 105 °C
T3: 120 °C

Experiments so far (best first):
B1 | L3 | S3 | C2 | T3 -> 59.8%
B3 | L4 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 49.1%
B2 | L5 | S3 | C1 | T3 -> 6.2%
B1 | L1 | S4 | C1 | T3 -> 0.0%
B2 | L7 | S2 | C1 | T1 -> 0.0%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"base": "<label>", "ligand": "<label>", "solvent": "<label>", "concentration": "<label>", "temperature": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: Tests whether a lower concentration improves the leading cesium pivalate/X-Phos/butyronitrile condition.
Tests whether higher concentration boosts the best observed condition.
Measures the effect of lowering temperature while holding the leading condition otherwise constant.
Tests whether a further temperature decrease improves selectivity or limits decomposition.
Tests whether the promising GorlosPhos result improves with the best observed base and concentration.
Isolates the effect of cesium acetate versus cesium pivalate with the leading ligand and solvent.
Tests potassium pivalate with the leading ligand and solvent to assess the counterion effect.
Tests potassium acetate against the cesium carboxylates under the leading catalyst conditions.
Screens bulky BrettPhos under the strongest observed base, solvent, concentration, and temperature.
Tests a chiral phosphite-type ligand in the leading reaction environment.
Screens the electron-rich JackiePhos ligand under the leading reaction conditions.
Tests a strongly donating trialkylphosphine ligand under the leading reaction conditions.
Assesses a compact, electron-rich phosphine as an alternative to X-Phos.
Evaluates triphenylphosphine as a less bulky ligand benchmark in the best solvent and base.
Revisits tBPh-CPhos with the leading base, solvent, and concentration to clarify its prior poor result.
Tests polar DMAc against the leading nitrile solvent while holding the catalyst conditions fixed.
Tests aromatic p-xylene with the leading base and ligand as a solvent comparison.
Reassesses n-butyl acetate using the leading ligand and concentration after its prior failure with a different ligand.
Tests whether the promising cesium acetate/GorlosPhos combination benefits from increasing concentration.
Directly compares cesium pivalate and cesium acetate with the promising GorlosPhos ligand.
